item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q021_nad_binding_convergent_evolution","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 shows that NAD(P) use is not evidence for one universal NAD(P)-enzyme ancestor. Examples include the Rossmann fold/superfamily c.2/c.2.1, the FAD/NAD(P)-binding fold c.3, the DHS-like NAD/FAD-binding fold c.31, the NAD(P)-linked oxidoreductase superfamily c.1.7 within the TIM barrel fold c.1, and the HMG-CoA-reductase NAD-binding superfamily d.58.20 within the ferredoxin-like fold d.58. Their occurrence in distinct folds—and even different structural classes, c (alpha/beta) versus d (alpha+beta)—supports repeated convergent recruitment of NAD(P) binding. This does not exclude divergence: members of one SCOPe family are relatively close homologs, while membership in one superfamily supports more remote common ancestry followed by divergence of sequence, substrate specificity, or reaction. Sharing only a fold does not establish homology because a SCOPe fold can contain evolutionarily unrelated superfamilies; class is still weaker and purely architectural.\n\nNAD(P) is ubiquitous, and its adenine, ribose, pyrophosphate, and nicotinamide groups impose recurring geometric and electrostatic constraints. Independent proteins can therefore converge on glycine-rich loops, beta-alpha nucleotide-binding elements, phosphate-binding residues, or similarly positioned catalytic residues. A local active-site match can likewise reflect chemical necessity rather than shared ancestry. Homology should instead be supported by concordant whole-domain evidence: significant sequence/profile similarity, extensive structural alignment with the same topology, conserved residue order and surrounding context, compatible insertions/deletions, mechanistic correspondence, and phylogenetic evidence. Cofactor binding or a few active-site residues alone must not be used to transfer SCOPe family/superfamily membership, substrate specificity, reaction, stereochemistry, domain boundaries, or catalytic annotations. Nor is a representative from one NAD(P)-binding fold automatically a safe modeling template for another; template choice requires global sequence/structure compatibility, and even a same-superfamily template does not by itself justify detailed function transfer.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info — /api/v1/; /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop — /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=NAD&mode=auto&limit=10","mcp__scope__get_scop_node — /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.1.7; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.1.7/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.2.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.2.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.3.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.3.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.31.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.31.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.58.20.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/d.58.20.1/parents"]}]}
